quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: You want to park uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels so your car will roll away from the road center if the brakes fail. Do this when parking uphill or downhill on a road without a curb.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
Stop and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, check for oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: If your tires lose contact with the road, you should:

options.text: Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.
Ease your foot off the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Ease off the gas and stay off the brakes until your tires grip the road again. Do not try to stop or turn.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Be ready for traffic to merge into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for traffic to merge into your lane.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you that traffic will merge from the right. Be prepared to safely allow merging traffic.

questions.question: When dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, slow down and turn on your:
questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever visibility is poor. This helps other drivers see you as well.

questions.question: When parked facing uphill on a street with a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn the wheels toward the curb.
Turn the wheels away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn wheels away from the curb when parked uphill with a curb present. Turn them toward the curb when parked downhill or uphill without a curb.

questions.question: What does a yellow pennant-shaped sign tell drivers?
questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: Yellow pennant signs mark no passing zones.

questions.question: You and another driver reach a four-way stop at the same time. The other driver is on your left. Who has the right-of-way?
questions.correctAnswerText: You.
questions.explanation: When two cars reach a four-way stop at the same time, the car to the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: What color are regulatory signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with black, red, or green letters or symbols. They inform drivers of traffic laws they must follow.

questions.question: A steady yellow light is ahead and you have not entered the intersection yet. You should:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means prepare to stop. If you haven't entered the intersection, come to a safe stop. If you're already in the intersection, clear it quickly.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice with Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), you should:

options.text: Press the brake pedal firmly and hold it.
Avoid brakes and let the car slow down on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal firmly and hold it.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly. The system will pump the brakes faster than you can.

questions.question: What do broken yellow lines indicate?

options.text: Same direction traffic in separate lanes.
Opposite direction traffic in separate lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opposite direction traffic in separate lanes.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Broken lines mean passing is allowed when safe.

questions.question: How far ahead of your vehicle should you look?
questions.correctAnswerText: One city block.
questions.explanation: Look at least one city block ahead to see potential hazards and avoid sudden stops or turns.

questions.question: When roads are slippery after rain starts, you should:

options.text: Test your tires' traction while going uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid fast turns and stops.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire traction. Slow down and avoid quick turns or stops to prevent skidding.

questions.question: A driver license is a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege that can be taken away if misused. All drivers must help keep roads safe.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, check traffic by:

options.text: Using your rearview and side mirrors.
Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic when entering a freeway. This helps you spot vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: Large trucks are likely to lose speed when:

options.text: Driving up long or steep hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more time to speed up than smaller vehicles. They lose speed going up long or steep hills. Leave extra space behind a truck, especially on hills.

questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are to your left and parked vehicles are to your right. You should steer:

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: Steer a middle course between the oncoming cars and the parked cars. This gives you the safest path.

questions.question: You are crossing an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with siren and flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.
questions.explanation: Continue through the intersection. Then drive to the right and stop. You must yield to emergency vehicles with sirens or flashing lights.

questions.question: If your car's rear end skids to the left, you should:

options.text: Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: Take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This straightens out your vehicle.

questions.question: Give the right-of-way to any pedestrian who is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians crossing the street in any marked or unmarked crosswalk. For safety, yield to people crossing any street.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows there is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.
Turn on your high beam headlights to better see the vehicles ahead of you.
Keep the instrument panel lights bright to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly at night because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop within the area your headlights light up.

questions.question: As you approach the top of a hill, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop, if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill or around a curve. Slow down so you can stop if needed. A vehicle could be stalled just out of sight.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:

options.text: Start to prepare to slow down.
Sound a sharp blast of your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound a sharp blast of your horn.
questions.explanation: Use a sharp blast on your horn when a child or pedestrian is about to enter the street in front of you.

questions.question: Defensive driving is:

options.text: Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
More dangerous than not driving defensively.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means using safe strategies to prevent crashes. You adjust your driving for weather, how you feel, and what other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians do.

questions.question: If you approach a flashing red traffic light, you:

options.text: Are traveling in the wrong direction.
Must treat the intersection as if it is controlled by a stop sign.
May not proceed until it changes to green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must treat the intersection as if it is controlled by a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all other traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: On a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means go. Turn in the direction the arrow points after you yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: Check your rearview mirrors:

options.text: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors frequently so you know where nearby vehicles are. Do not stare in one direction.

questions.question: If your car begins to skid out of control, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes during a skid. Keep steering until your vehicle is back under control and moving safely.
